How many counties does Indiana have, and why does that matter when you sell?

Indiana has 92 counties, and almost every step of a house sale runs through one of them. The county treasurer collects your tax bill, the county recorder files your deed, and the county auditor and assessor handle the paperwork that follows a sale. Which office you call depends on where the house sits, so the county matters more than the mailing address.

Counties vary a great deal in size. Marion County, home to Indianapolis, has 992,196 residents, while Ohio County has 5,994. Allen County is the largest by area at 657 square miles and Ohio County the smallest at 86. Each county is run by two bodies, a county council and a board of commissioners.

When are Indiana property taxes due, and who do you pay?

Property tax in Indiana is billed twice a year and paid to your county treasurer. The state Department of Local Government Finance lists the current due dates as May 11, 2026 and November 10, 2026.

Late payment carries a penalty that grows quickly. Pay within 30 days of the due date, with no back taxes owed on the same parcel, and the penalty is 5 percent of the unpaid amount. Miss that window and it rises to 10 percent.

  • Call the county treasurer for the amount due and any past-due balance on the parcel.
  • Call the county auditor if you want to confirm which deductions are on the property.
  • Ask the title company to order a payoff figure before closing, since unpaid tax is usually settled from the sale proceeds.

If you are behind, selling is still possible. Our Indiana property tax guide covers appeals and selling with tax due, and the tax lien page and tax sale page explain what happens when a balance goes unpaid for longer.

What happens to the homestead deduction when you sell?

The homestead standard deduction lowers the assessed value of the home you live in, and it is shrinking. Under Indiana Code 6-1.1-12-37, the deduction for assessment dates after December 31, 2024 steps down each year until it reaches zero in 2030.

Assessment yearStandard deduction
2025$48,000
2026$40,000
2027$30,000
2028$20,000
2029$10,000
2030 and later$0

Before 2025 the deduction was the lesser of 60 percent of assessed value or $48,000. Only one standard deduction applies to a homestead for an assessment date, and the county auditor records it. The next owner's bill can therefore look different from yours. Our homestead exemption guide walks through filing and what changes after a sale.

How does foreclosure work in Indiana, and can you sell before the sheriff's sale?

Foreclosure in Indiana goes through a court, and a sale can only happen after a judgment. Lenders must also give notice first. For foreclosure actions filed after June 30, 2009, the creditor has to send the borrower a presuit notice by certified mail at least 30 days before filing. The notice tells the borrower about default and encourages contact with a foreclosure counselor.

Once the complaint is filed, the clock is slower than most owners expect. For a mortgage signed after June 30, 1975, process to carry out the sale cannot issue until three months after the complaint is filed. The exception is a house a court finds abandoned, where the sale can be carried out on the day of judgment.

Until the sale, the owner can still redeem the house from the judgment. Under IC 32-29-7-7, that means paying the judgment amount, interest and costs to the clerk, or to the sheriff once the judgment has been issued to the sheriff.

  • Ask the title company for a payoff figure that includes fees, since the lender's number changes during a case.
  • Do not wait for the sale date. A closing has to finish before the sheriff sells the property.

We explain the sale steps and redemption in our sheriff sale guide.

How do you sell an inherited house in Indiana?

Indiana repealed its inheritance tax in 2013, and the Department of Revenue states that no inheritance tax is owed. The tax applied only to people who died on or before December 31, 2012, and no returns should be filed after October 5, 2023.

Small estates get a lighter process. Under IC 29-1-8-3, if the gross probate estate, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $100,000 plus administration costs and reasonable funeral expenses for a person who died after June 30, 2022, the fiduciary can distribute without giving notice to creditors. Check the numbers with the probate court clerk or an estate attorney.

  • Gather the death certificate, the will if there is one, and the deed.
  • Ask the county clerk where the estate is filed.
  • Confirm who has authority to sign the deed before you accept any offer.

Our pages on Indiana probate, estate and inheritance tax and transfer on death deeds cover the rest. If the house was left by a deed outside probate, the quitclaim deed page explains what that document does and does not pass on.

What paperwork and fees come with closing and recording a deed?

Two county steps follow every Indiana sale. First, before the deed goes to the county auditor, all parties complete and sign a sales disclosure form prescribed by the Department of Local Government Finance. The rule covers deeds, contracts of sale and transfers by foreclosure, divorce, court order or probate, and it does not cover mortgages.

Second, the deed is recorded with the county recorder. Indiana Code 36-2-7-10 sets a $25 fee for recording a deed or other instrument that is not a mortgage, and $55 for a mortgage. Counties can add small charges by ordinance, so ask for the total before you wire anything.

What if tenants live in the house you want to sell?

A tenant does not have to leave just because the house is listed, and the lease terms follow the property. Indiana Code 32-31-1-6 says a landlord may end a lease for unpaid rent with at least 10 days notice, unless the parties agreed otherwise or the tenant pays in full before the notice runs out.

  • Read the lease for its end date and any notice terms.

Some buyers will take a house with tenants in place and some prefer it vacant, which is worth asking about on the first call. Our eviction process page and landlord and tenant guide cover the court steps and what a sale does to a lease.

What does selling as-is for cash mean in Indiana?

An as-is cash sale means the buyer takes the house in its current condition and does not ask you to fix, clean or update it first. There is no mortgage approval to wait on, so closing is set by how fast the title work and your own paperwork are ready. The county steps above still apply: the sales disclosure form, the tax payoff and the recording.

One Indiana issue worth testing for is radon. According to the American Lung Association, every Indiana county sits in EPA Zone 1 or Zone 2, which means a medium to high potential for elevated radon. The Indiana Radon HelpLine is 1-800-272-9723, and some counties offer free test kits through the local health department.

Other repair issues vary by region and by house, so we leave them out here. If you tell us the county and what is wrong with the property, we can say what to expect. Our Indiana guides by city and county page lists the rest of our Indiana library, and the land contract page is worth a look if you sold on payments years ago.

Frequently asked questions

How many counties are in Indiana?

Indiana has 92 counties.

When are Indiana property taxes due?

The state lists May 11, 2026 and November 10, 2026. Pay within 30 days of the due date and the penalty is 5 percent of the unpaid tax, then 10 percent after that.

Does Indiana have an inheritance tax?

No. The Department of Revenue says the tax was repealed in 2013 and that no inheritance tax is owed.

How long does an Indiana foreclosure take?

For a mortgage made after June 30, 1975, process to sell cannot issue until three months after the complaint is filed, and the lender must send a presuit notice 30 days earlier.

Can I sell my house before the sheriff sells it?

Yes, as long as the closing finishes before the sale. An owner can also redeem before the sale by paying the judgment, interest and costs.

Do I need a sales disclosure form?

Usually yes. The parties sign it before the deed is filed with the county auditor. Ask the auditor or the title company which form your parcel needs.
